About Latch

Latch turns how people actually do their work into automations, without a single prompt. Show Latch a task and talk it through; it captures the steps, exceptions and reasoning, then builds sidekicks that run the work the same way every time and stop to ask when a decision needs a person. That knowledge is also available to any AI agent over MCP. Founded by Stefan Kalb and Jared Kofron, Latch is based in Seattle and backed by Fuse, Soma Capital, Garry Tan, Liquid 2 Ventures and Pioneer Fund. Learn more at latch.ai.

## Recommended Stories [...] Unlike most AI tools, which at most capture screenshots or record video to get a deeper understanding of work, Latch actually asks questions, eliciting information about what happens when processes differ from written procedure. Employees just show Latch a task while Latch watches and asks questions, building institutional context about what happens when the process isn't clear. Latch then builds a "sidekick" that automates the work to save time, reduce errors, and turn the focus to the interpretation of the results.

Latch's own finance team turned a month-end Xero-to-Google Sheets workflow into a scheduled sidekick, cutting more than 200 clicks to about a dozen and saving 15 minutes of manual work per run. [...] "AI can be a game changer to automate financial and accounting workflows. But securely implementing AI across your team can be difficult and costly, especially when that process involves significant investment from your IT team. Latch understands natural language and video intuitively, asking questions the same way a human teammate would, and uses that as the basis of building useful AI automations."  
-Stefan Kalb, Cofounder and CEO, Latch

results.title: Introducing Latch V2 — Your AI CFO. | Latch
results.content:
1. Connect. Link QuickBooks Online, your bank, your CRM, payroll, and any spend tools you use. Latch reads everything automatically from there. No manual entry. No setup calls required.

2. Configure by text. Latch introduces itself and runs a short onboarding conversation — communication style, target margins, payroll cadence, busy season, known issues, growth plans. Every answer trains the agent and goes into your account's working memory. The next time it surfaces an insight, it does it the way you asked.

3. Get to work. Latch handles the routine monitoring automatically. Anything risky, unclear, or actionable gets flagged to you by text — with the dollar impact and a recommended next move. [...] Latch V2 fixes that. It's the AI CFO purpose-built for home service contractors, and it runs in the one place you already live: a text thread.

# Not software. A hire.

Latch isn't a tool you log into. It's a hire you put to work.

Most financial software is built around the same broken loop: collect data, build a dashboard, hope someone reads it. Latch flips the model. It plugs into your books, bank, CRM, payroll, and spend tools — then continuously monitors every transaction, every job, every dollar in or out. When something matters, it texts you. With the numbers, the context, and the recommended action.

It's the work a $200,000-a-year CFO and controller would do — without the salary, the equity, or the 90-day ramp. [...] No. And on purpose.

Latch doesn't do data entry. It doesn't file taxes. It doesn't run payroll or pay bills. Those jobs still belong to your bookkeeper, your CPA, and your payroll provider — because they should.

What Latch does is sit on top of all of it and make every one of those people more accurate, more accountable, and more useful. It catches the bookkeeper's miscoded entries. It flags the AR your office manager forgot to chase. It tells you when the duplicate vendor charge slipped through your AP review.

The pitch is simple: keep your bookkeeper. Latch makes them 3x better by catching every mistake, automating every report, and giving you a controller on top to make sure nothing falls through the cracks.
